numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When using statsmodels.tsa.ardl.UECM.from_ardl, the residuals method of the resulting UECM subtracts the fitted values of the UECM (in differences) from the endogenous value of the ARDL (in levels), producing incorrect residuals (uecmfit.resid) that differ from the equivalent ARDL residuals (ardlfit.resid).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The UECM should have the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL, since no transformation is made to the residuals in deriving the UECM from the ARDL.
trigger_conditions: Create a UECM from a fitted ARDL using statsmodels.tsa.ardl.UECM.from_ardl(ardl).
Call fit() on the resulting UECM and access the residuals method/property (uecmfit.resid).
Residual computation mixes UECM fitted values in differences with the ARDL endogenous value in levels (the mismatch described in issue #9323).

input_output_examples.input:
Simulate cointegrated series with w=[1,-1], N=100, S initialized as np.ones([N,len(w)])*2000, kappa=20, sigma=20, dt=1/N, corr=0.6; build S by iterating t=1..N-1 using the code in issue #9323; then fit:
ardl = sm.tsa.ARDL(S[:,[0]], 1, S[:,[1]], 1)
ardlfit = ardl.fit()
uecm = sm.tsa.UECM.from_ardl(ardl)
uecmfit = uecm.fit(); then evaluate uecmfit.resid (observed) and ardlfit.resid (expected), and check S[:,0].squeeze() == uecmfit.model.endog.squeeze().
input_output_examples.buggy_output: uecmfit.resid (incorrect residuals because it subtracts UECM fitted values in differences from the ARDL endogenous value in levels).
input_output_examples.expected_output: uecmfit.resid should equal ardlfit.resid (since no residual transformation should occur when deriving the UECM from the ARDL).

oracle_clues: Issue #9323 states the correctness requirement explicitly: “The UECM should have the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL, since no transformation is made to the residuals in deriving the UECM from the ARDL.”

PR #9390 description indicates the fix: “Override resid property to compute correct residuals” and changes resid computation to use `model._y - self.fittedvalues` (implying the previously incorrect residual computation is rectified).
The issue’s provided code compares uecmfit.resid (observed) against ardlfit.resid (expected).

category_specific_evidence: UECM residuals are computed inconsistently with ARDL residuals: the UECM residuals subtract the UECM fitted values (in differences) from the ARDL endogenous value (in levels), causing residuals to differ even though no residual transformation should occur when deriving UECM from ARDL (issue #9323).
Issue #9323 describes an equality requirement: “The UECM should have the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL, since no transformation is made to the residuals in deriving the UECM from the ARDL.”

The provided code sample computes `uecmfit.resid` (observed) and `ardlfit.resid` (expected) and intends the check: `# check equality of UECM endog variable and observation in levels` via `S[:,0].squeeze() == uecmfit.model.endog.squeeze()` (issue #9323).
PR fix: “Override resid property to compute correct residuals” and code change adds `resid` as `model._y - self.fittedvalues` (statsmodels/tsa/ardl/model.py diff around resid).
reproduction_risks: The only concrete numeric values in the passage are for the simulation setup (e.g., w=[1,-1], N=100, S initialized to 2000, kappa=20, sigma=20, dt=1/N, corr=0.6). The passage does not provide explicit residual numeric outputs or an explicit numeric tolerance/check for equality.
The actual failing behavior is described conceptually (differences vs levels mismatch) but the passage does not provide concrete residual arrays or norms used to demonstrate the violation.

The fix references `model._y - self.fittedvalues`; without full context of how `fittedvalues` are computed (levels vs differences) the reproduction may need to ensure the same configuration as in the issue example.

provenance.value: The residuals from statsmodels.tsa.UECM.fit() (accessed via uecmfit.resid / the residuals method) subtract fitted values of the UECM in differences from the ARDL endogenous value in levels, producing incorrect residuals that differ from the ARDL residuals.
The UECM residuals should be the same as the equivalent ARDL residuals, since no transformation is made to the residuals when deriving the UECM from the ARDL.

When using statsmodels.tsa.ardl.UECM.from_ardl, the residuals method of the resulting UECM subtracts the fitted values of the UECM (in differences) from the endogenous value of the ARDL (in levels), producing incorrect residuals (uecmfit.resid) that differ from the equivalent ARDL residuals (ardlfit.resid).
The UECM should have the same residuals as the equivalent ARDL, since no transformation is made to the residuals in deriving the UECM from the ARDL.
